title: Treasury Standard — Face Amount of a Replacement Capital Credit Check
content:
# Face Amount of a Replacement Capital Credit Check

**Treasury standard — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).**

## Clause

The face of a replacement check is the voided amount of the most recently voided check, the amount that void returned to the amount owed, with nothing deducted; the face is rounded half up to the cent. A face is never below zero. With nothing deducted, the charges recorded with the replacement total 0.00.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Most recently voided check | the latest void entry on the capital account, by entry date |
| Voided amount | the amount of that void entry, which the void returned to the retired credits owed on the account |
| Face | the amount printed on the replacement check |
| Charges recorded | the total recorded with the replacement as deducted from it, rounded half up to the cent |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

| Void history on the account | Face of the replacement | Charges recorded |
|---|---|---|
| one check of $86.40 voided as stale-dated | $86.40 | 0.00 |
| a check of $52.10 voided as lost, its replacement later voided as returned undeliverable for $52.10 | $52.10, the most recent void | 0.00 |
| a $40.00 check voided last spring, then a $63.25 check voided last month | $63.25 | 0.00 |

The face always follows the most recent void entry, not the original payout and not an earlier void.
